opportunities.title: Cisco's Email Gateway Has a Root-Access Problem, and Attackers Already Have the Keys
opportunities.why_now: A max-severity Cisco Secure Email Gateway RCE is under active exploitation right now, confirmed independently by SecurityWeek, The Hacker News, and Bleeping Computer within hours of each other.
opportunities.angle: Breaking-patch alert format: what the CVE does, indicators of compromise, and a hard patch-now deadline for admins

opportunities.title: GitLab's Perfect 10 Wasn't Perfect Enough: Exploits Landed Before Most Admins Even Patched
opportunities.why_now: A CVSS 10.0 GitLab flaw is already being weaponized in the wild just days after the fix shipped, exposing how thin the patch-to-exploit window has gotten for supply-chain-critical tools.
opportunities.angle: Patch-cadence teardown: timeline from disclosure to exploitation, plus a supply-chain blast-radius estimate for self-hosted GitLab instances

opportunities.title: Sandworm Is Back Inside Cisco Gear, and Cyclops Blink Never Really Left
opportunities.why_now: Dark Reading confirms the Russian GRU-linked Sandworm crew is chaining multiple Cisco vulnerabilities to redeploy its Cyclops Blink implant, a threat that DOJ/CISA thought they'd disrupted years ago.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor profile refresh: what changed in the Cisco exploit chain, why Cyclops Blink keeps resurrecting, and what network defenders should hunt for

opportunities.title: DDRop Just Broke the 'Confidential' in Confidential Computing
opportunities.why_now: A new hardware attack (DDRop) is reported to defeat both Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP, the two flagship confidential-computing protections cloud providers have sold as unbreakable for years.
opportunities.angle: Explainer with stakes: how the attack works at the DRAM level, which cloud workloads are exposed, and whether any mitigation exists yet

opportunities.title: Passkeys Were Supposed to Kill Phishing. Attackers Found the Workaround.
opportunities.why_now: Just as UK.gov begins retiring passwords for 23 million users, The Hacker News reports active campaigns using passkey phishing to hijack Microsoft cloud accounts, undercutting the industry's core passwordless promise.
opportunities.angle: Counter-narrative piece pairing the UK passwordless rollout with the new bypass technique, framed as a reality-check for phishing-resistant auth claims
